chunks: From him, from Aḥmad, from al-Barqī, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade relieving oneself on the edge of a water well from which sweet water is drawn, or by a river from which water is sought, or beneath a tree bearing its fruit.

key_terms.بِئْرِ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.شَفِيرِ: the edge or brink of something, here the side of a well
key_terms.نَهَى: he prohibited; indicates a forbiddance in legal context
key_terms.يُسْتَعْذَبُ: from which fresh or palatable water is sought

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbid regarding relieving oneself near water sources and fruit trees?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم prohibited defecating near sources of usable water and beneath fruit-bearing trees. It reflects Islamic legal and ethical concern for taharah (ritual purity), public welfare, and protection from harm and contamination.
